words.gloss: studied through reliance on a book
in the midst of an assembly

hindi: पुस्तक के भरोसे पढ़ा हुआ, गुरु के समीप न पढ़ा हुआ, सभा के बीच शोभा नहीं देते, उपपति से गर्भवती स्त्रियों के समान।
english: Studied through reliance on a book, not studied in a teacher's presence, they do not shine in the midst of an assembly, like women pregnant by a paramour.
notes: śobhante is plural while adhītam is neuter singular; the subject is not stated and none is supplied beyond the plural verb. pratyaya = reliance. jāra-garbhā: bahuvrīhi, literally 'having a paramour's embryo'.

hindi: किए हुए के बदले प्रतिकार करे; हिंसा में प्रतिहिंसा करे। वहाँ दोष नहीं पड़ता; बुरे के प्रति बुरा आचरण करना चाहिए।
english: For a deed done, one should do a requital; in harming, counter-harm. A fault does not fall there. Toward a bad one, one should act badly.
notes: In line a pratihiṃsanam has no verb of its own and shares kuryāt. duṣṭe is taken as locative 'toward a bad one' (m.); duṣṭam as the adverbial accusative 'badly'.

hindi: जो दूर है, जो कठिनाई से प्राप्त होने योग्य है और जो दूर स्थित है, वह सब तप से साधने योग्य है; तप निश्चय ही दुरतिक्रम है, जिसे लाँघना कठिन है।
english: What is far, what is hard to attain, and what stands far away, all that is to be accomplished by austerity; austerity is indeed hard to overcome.
notes: durārādhya: 'hard to propitiate / hard to win'; rendered 'hard to attain'. The relative yat is printed three times and kept each time.

hindi: यदि लोभ है, अवगुण से क्या? यदि चुगलखोरी है, पापों से क्या? और यदि सत्य है, तप से क्या? यदि मन पवित्र है, तीर्थ से क्या? यदि सज्जनता है, गुणों से क्या? यदि बड़ी महिमा है, आभूषणों से क्या? यदि उत्तम विद्या है, धन से क्या? यदि अपयश है, मृत्यु से क्या?
english: If there is greed, what need of vice? If there is slander, what need of sins? And if there is truth, what need of austerity? If the mind is pure, what need of a holy place? If there is goodness, what need of virtues? If there is great renown, what need of ornaments? If there is good learning, what need of wealth? If there is ill fame, what need of death?
notes: kim with the instrumental = 'what need of'. The single ca in line b stands after tapasā; it is rendered as 'And' at the head of its clause, since it joins the clause to the preceding ones. aguṇa = absence of virtue, rendered 'vice'. saujanya = the quality of a good man (sajjana).

hindi: जिसके पिता रत्नाकर हैं, जिसकी बहन लक्ष्मी है, वह शंख भिक्षाटन करे; जो दिया नहीं गया वह उपस्थित नहीं होता।
english: The conch, whose father is Ratnākara, the mine of jewels, whose sister is Lakṣmī, would go about begging; what is not given does not present itself.
notes: ratnākara = mine of jewels; the ocean is understood from the context but not named. 'na dattam upatiṣṭhate' is read as 'what is not given does not present itself' (na negating dattam as a unit with the verb); the line's sense is that nothing comes unless given. sahodarā = born of the same womb, here a sister.

hindi: पर असमर्थ साधु हो; निर्धन ब्रह्मचारी; रोगी देवभक्त और वृद्ध नारी पतिव्रता।
english: But a powerless one would be a good man; a penniless one a celibate student; a sick one devoted to the gods, and an old woman devoted to her husband.

text_flags.why: possible: the pairs of this verse run in parallel and the following pair has ca; vā between brahmacārī and nirdhanaḥ breaks the pairing

notes: The pairing is powerless = good man, penniless = celibate student, sick = devoted to the gods, old woman = devoted to her husband. vā in line a sits between brahmacārī and nirdhanaḥ and breaks the pairing (the other pairs are joined by ca or by nothing); it is left untranslated and flagged as a possible ca. bhavet is shared by all four pairs.

hindi: अन्न और जल के समान दान नहीं; द्वादशी के समान तिथि नहीं; गायत्री से श्रेष्ठ मन्त्र नहीं; माता से श्रेष्ठ देवता नहीं।
english: There is no giving equal to food and water; no lunar day equal to the twelfth; no mantra higher than the Gāyatrī; no deity higher than the mother.
notes: anna-udaka is a dvandva (food and water). gāyatryāḥ and mātuḥ are ablatives of comparison. mantra here is a ritual formula, not counsel.

hindi: तक्षक का विष दाँत में है, पर मक्खी का सिर में; बिच्छू का विष पूँछ में; दुर्जन में सारे शरीर में विष है।
english: Takṣaka's poison is in the tooth, but a fly's is in the head; a scorpion's poison is in the tail; in the wicked man there is poison in the whole body.
notes: Takṣaka is kept as a name; that he is a serpent is inferred only from 'poison in the tooth'. sarvāṅga: 'whole body' (aṅga = limb/body). No verb is printed; 'is' is supplied in English and Hindi for the nominal clauses.

hindi: पति की आज्ञा के बिना नारी निश्चय ही उपवास करके व्रत का आचरण करती हुई पति की आयु हर लेती है; वह नारी नरक में जाए।
english: Without her husband's command, a woman indeed, having fasted, practising a vow, takes away her husband's life-span; that woman would go to hell.
notes: ājñā = command, permission. vinā governs the accusative ājñām here. upoṣya is the absolutive of √vas 'to fast' (upa-√vas).

hindi: नारी दानों से शुद्ध नहीं होती, सैकड़ों उपवासों से भी नहीं; तीर्थसेवा से उस प्रकार नहीं जैसे पति के चरणोदक से।
english: A woman is not purified by gifts, not even by hundreds of fasts; not by frequenting holy places, in like manner as by her husband's foot-water.
notes: tadvat ... yathā is a correlative pair ('in like manner as'). The verb śudhyate is carried over to line b. pada-udaka = water in which the feet were washed.

hindi: पाँव का शेष, पिए हुए का शेष, सन्ध्या का शेष और वैसे ही; कुत्ते के मूत्र के समान जल पीकर चान्द्रायण करे।
english: Remnant of the foot, remnant of what was drunk, remnant of the twilight rite, and just so: having drunk water equal to a dog's urine, one should perform the cāndrāyaṇa.
notes: pāda-śeṣa is taken literally as 'remnant of the foot'; the text does not say 'foot-water', though that is the evident sense. The three śeṣa words qualify toyam in line b. cāndrāyaṇa is the name of a penance (lunar).

hindi: हाथ दान से, पर कंकण से नहीं; शुद्धि स्नान से, पर चन्दन से नहीं; तृप्ति मान से, पर भोजन से नहीं; मुक्ति ज्ञान से, पर मुण्डन से नहीं।
english: The hand by giving, but not by a bracelet; purity by bathing, but not by sandal-paste; satisfaction by honour, but not by food; liberation by knowledge, but not by shaving the head.
notes: No verb is printed in any of the four lines and none is supplied. māna = honour (alternatively respect or pride). muṇḍana = shaving of the head.

hindi: नाई के घर में हजामत, पत्थर पर गन्ध का लेपन, जल में अपना रूप देखना, शक्र की भी लक्ष्मी को हर ले।
english: Shaving in a barber's house, anointing with scent on a stone, looking at one's own form in water would take away even Śakra's fortune.
notes: The construction is elliptical: kṣauram and gandhalepanam have no verb, and paśyan is a masculine participle; the three acts are taken together as the subject of haret. Śakra is kept as a name.

hindi: तुण्डी तत्काल प्रज्ञा हर लेती है, वचा तत्काल प्रज्ञा उत्पन्न करती है; नारी तत्काल शक्ति हर लेती है, दूध तत्काल शक्ति उत्पन्न करता है।
english: Tuṇḍī at once takes away wisdom; Vacā at once produces wisdom; woman at once takes away power; milk at once produces power.
notes: Tuṇḍī and Vacā are kept as names and not identified. payas = milk (it can also mean water).

hindi: जिन सज्जनों के हृदय में परोपकार जागता है, उनकी विपत्तियाँ नष्ट होती हैं, पद-पद पर सम्पत्तियाँ हों।
english: Of the good in whose heart helping others is awake, their misfortunes perish; prosperity would be at every step.
notes: pade pade = 'at every step' (repetition). sampadaḥ is plural; rendered 'prosperity'. syuḥ is optative 'would be'.

words.gloss: endowed with the virtue of humility
in the city of the best of gods

hindi: यदि मनोहर स्त्री, और यदि रमा, यदि विनय के गुण से युक्त पुत्र, पुत्र में पुत्र का जन्म, तो देवश्रेष्ठ के नगर में क्या अधिकता?
english: If a charming woman, and if Ramā, if a son endowed with the virtue of humility, the birth of a son in the son: in the city of the best of gods, what superiority?
notes: rāmā (charming woman) and ramā (Ramā, a name of Lakṣmī, i.e. fortune) are a deliberate near-pun. vinaya can also be discipline or modesty. sura-vara-nagara: 'city of the best of gods' (suravara read as a tat-puruṣa); an alternative is 'excellent city of the gods'. No verb is printed in the yadi clauses. tanaye tanayotpattiḥ is read as 'the birth of a son in the son' (a grandson).

hindi: आहार, निद्रा, भय और मैथुन; और ये मनुष्यों के, पशुओं के एक-से हैं। ज्ञान मनुष्यों की अधिक विशेषता है; ज्ञान से हीन पशुओं के समान हैं।
english: Eating, sleep, fear and copulation: and these are equal for men, for beasts. Knowledge is the additional distinction of men; devoid of knowledge, they are equal to beasts.
notes: nṛṇām paśūnām stand side by side without ca (asyndeton). hīnāḥ samānāḥ have no stated subject; 'they' refers to men. adhika viśeṣa = additional (further) distinction.

words.gloss: by the flapping of the ears
with a mind blinded by rut
loss of the adornment of the pair of temples
in a forest of blossoming lotuses

hindi: यदि दान चाहने वाले भौंरे कानों की फड़फड़ाहट से दूर कर दिए गए, श्रेष्ठ हाथी द्वारा मद से अन्धी बुद्धि से दूर कर दिए गए, यह उसी के दोनों गण्डस्थलों की शोभा की हानि है; भौंरे फिर खिले कमलों के वन में बसते हैं।
english: If the bees seeking dāna (rut-fluid) are driven away by the flapping of his ears, driven away by the best of elephants with a mind blinded by rut, this is the loss of the adornment of his own pair of temples alone; the bees again dwell in a forest of blossoming lotuses.
notes: dāna means both 'gift' and the rut-fluid of an elephant; the sense 'rut-fluid' is taken from karivara and gaṇḍa. mada = rut (also intoxication or pride). gaṇḍa = temple or cheek of the elephant. bhṛṃgāḥ is the printed spelling of bhṛṅgāḥ (anusvāra before g) and is not treated as an error. dūrīkṛtāḥ is repeated deliberately in line b.

hindi: राजा, वेश्या, यम और अग्नि, चोर, बालक और याचक दूसरे का दुःख नहीं जानते; आठवाँ ग्रामकण्टक है।
english: King, courtesan, Yama and fire, thief, child and beggar do not know another's sorrow; the eighth is the village-thorn.
notes: Count: king, courtesan, Yama, fire, thief, child, beggar are seven; the village-thorn is the eighth. bāla-yācakau is a dual dvandva (two members). Yama is kept as a name.

hindi: हे बाले, तुम नीचे क्यों देखती हो? पृथ्वी पर तुम्हारा क्या गिरा है? अरे अरे मूर्ख, तुम नहीं जानते: यौवन का मोती चला गया है।
english: Why do you look down, girl? What of yours has fallen on the ground? Ho, ho, fool, you do not know: the pearl of youth has gone.
notes: The verse is a dialogue: the first two questions are put to the girl, and 're re mūrkha' is the reply of the second speaker; no speaker is named. The first kim can be 'why' or a mere question particle.

hindi: साँपों के आश्रय वाली भी, फलरहित भी, काँटों वाली भी, टेढ़ी भी, कीचड़ में उत्पन्न भी, कठिनता से पहुँचने योग्य भी, हे केतकी, तुम गन्ध से सब प्राणियों को सुन्दर हो; एक गुण निश्चय ही सब दोषों को नष्ट करता है।
english: Even with serpents as refuge, even fruitless, even thorny, even crooked, even born in mud, even hard to approach, you are charming by fragrance, Ketakī, to every creature; one virtue indeed destroys all faults.
notes: Line c ends with a hyphen (sarvajanto-) and line d begins reko: the split is sarvajantoḥ + ekaḥ (visarga becomes r before the next line's vowel). The genitive sarvajantoḥ is taken with bandhurā ('charming to every creature'); the alternative is to join it with the next clause. vyāla can mean serpent or beast of prey. Ketakī is kept as a name and addressed; not identified.
